title: Answer to Question: Iran's Role in the Region
text:
(Series of answers of the eminent scholar Ata Bin Khalil Abu al-Rashtah, Amir of Hizb ut Tahrir, to the questions of visitors to his Facebook page "Political")

Answer to Question:
Iran's Role in the Region

To Mais Bader

Question:

Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. My master, the eminent Sheikh, may Allah protect you and take care of you. The question: Why has the United States of America allowed Iran this relatively rapid escalation of its diverse military capabilities, such that it has become one of the most important states in the region in terms of playing roles influential on the course of events in Iraq, Syria, the Gulf and the inflamed region in general? And what is the policy of the Americans in containing this unrestrained role? May Allah reward you with good...

Answer:

1- The saying that Iran has an unrestrained role in the region is a misplaced saying. Iran goes along with America in all the issues of the region... Iran is a central state in American policy in the region, and America relies on it in Iraq, Syria, Yemen, Afghanistan and Lebanon, and elsewhere... Whoever looks into Iran's actions with careful consideration finds that clear. More than one of the Iranian leaders has stated that Iran's cooperation with America is what enabled it to occupy Afghanistan and Iraq... and likewise in the other issues.

2- We issued an Answer to Question on the fourteenth of Shawwal 1434 AH, corresponding to 21/08/2013 CE, entitled: "The reality of Iran in relation to American policy?", in which we explained in detail the reality of Iran's relationship with America and Iran's cooperation with it in the issues of the region. You can refer to it to see what came in it, and I extract for you from it the following:

(- All the political actions in the region which Iran has undertaken all take place in accord and harmony with the American projects:

- In Lebanon it founded a party for itself from the followers of its madhhab and armed it, so it became a private army there separate from the Lebanese army, and the Lebanese regime recognised it and its weapons, knowing that the Lebanese regime is a secular regime following American policy. And the Lebanese regime did not allow other parties to bear arms, or did not recognise the weapons of the other parties. And Iran's party in Lebanon supported the Syrian regime linked to America, as Iran did, and America did not prevent the Lebanese regime from allowing Iran's party to intervene in Syria to back the secular regime of Bashar Assad there; rather, there is implicit American approval of this party's intervention in Syria without the Lebanese army obstructing it.

- When America occupied Iraq it met resistance it did not expect, so it brought Iran into Iraq to help it by influencing those belonging to its madhhab, so as to influence them and prevent them from moving against the occupation; rather, to make them stand against the resistance, confront it, and give legitimacy to the occupation and to the regime it established there, especially after 2005 when America allowed the coalition of parties supporting Iran to come to power under the premiership of Ibrahim al-Jaafari and then al-Maliki. These governments were founded by America and are linked to it, and the government of al-Maliki, which Iran backs, signed the security and strategic agreements with America to preserve its influence after the formal end of its occupation of Iraq, which indicates American satisfaction with the Iranian role, whose officials have admitted cooperating with America in the occupation of Iraq and in working to secure stability for American influence in Iraq. Iran opened an embassy in Iraq directly after the occupation, and no sooner was al-Jaafari elected than the Iranian Foreign Minister at the time, Kamal Kharrazi, visited Baghdad in 2005, at the height of the occupation. The two sides condemned the acts of resistance to the occupation under the name of condemning terrorism in Iraq. And al-Jaafari visited Iran and signed numerous agreements, among them an agreement of cooperation in the field of intelligence between them to establish security and monitor the crossings and borders, and to link Basra to the Iranian electricity network and build an oil pipeline between Basra and Abadan...

- As for Iran's relationship with the Syrian regime, it is old, dating from the outbreak of the first uprising at the beginning of the eighties of the last century, when it supported the Syrian regime in its suppression of the Muslim people of Syria in that era, so as to preserve it within the American project supporting the regime under the leadership of its agents, the Assad family. And it knows that it is a secular, Baathist, nationalist regime, the twin of the regime of Saddam which it used to fight, which has no relation to Islam; rather, it fights Islam and its people. And it realises that it is linked to America. So it did not undertake the defence of the rights of the Muslims; rather, it did the opposite: it fought them and supported a criminal regime of Kufr, and it is still doing so. The Iranian regime maintains close relations with the Syrian leadership, and these relations included military, economic and political relations. Iran has transferred many weapons to support the Assad regime and provided it with oil and gas at reduced prices given the absence of energy reserves in Syria. The political relations can be noticed in particular in the Iranian intervention in the Syrian uprising when the Assad regime was on the verge of collapse; and were it not for the Iranian intervention by sending forces of the Revolutionary Guard, the forces of Iran's party and the militias of al-Maliki that follow Iran, were it not for that, Bashar and his regime would have collapsed. The massacres of al-Qusayr and Homs, and today the chemical massacres of Ghouta and others, are witnesses to that intervention.

- In Afghanistan Iran supported the American occupation and supported the constitution it drew up and the government it formed under the presidency of Karzai, in service of America, and Iran secured the north of the country when America failed to defeat the Taliban. The former President of the Iranian Republic, Rafsanjani, mentioned: "Had our forces not helped in fighting the Taliban, the Americans would have drowned in the Afghan quagmire." (Asharq al-Awsat newspaper 9/2/2002). And Mohammad Ali Abtahi, the deputy of the former Iranian President Khatami for legal and parliamentary affairs, mentioned at the conference "The Gulf and the Challenges of the Future" held in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi on the evening of 13/1/2004; he said: "Were it not for Iranian cooperation, Kabul and Baghdad would not have fallen so easily. But we received a reward and became part of the axis of evil"! (IslamOnline.net 13/1/2004). And President Ahmadinejad had repeated the like of that during his visit to New York to attend the United Nations meetings, in an interview with the New York Times on 26/9/2008, where he said: "Iran extended a helping hand to the United States regarding Afghanistan, and the result of this help was the American President directing direct threats to launch a military attack against us. Our country also provided help to America in restoring calm and stability to Iraq.") End.

3- Bearing witness to all of the above is what the matter of the nuclear negotiations has ended in, and America's insistence on closing this file in order to improve open relations with Iran, so as to implement the role that America draws up for it in the region on the pretext of common interests, and without cover, not even a thin veil as was the case previously! The American President delivered a speech in front of the White House devoted to talking about the latest nuclear agreement with Iran, in which he described the agreement as "good, meeting our basic objectives", and he said: "As for the Iranian people, we are ready to work for the common interest" (American Radio Sawa 2/4/2015)... So it is clear in the American President's statements that he wants to work with Iran under the name of common interest! And what common interest is there with the Great Satan except the realisation of the American projects in the region?!

4- Then there is what has taken place and is taking place of harmonised plans between America, Iran and the Houthis in the events of Yemen! As for the Houthis' relationship with Iran, it needs no proof; it is more famous than a mountain with a fire on its peak... As for America's support for the Houthis, every person of sight and insight realises it. America acts in Yemen with its well-known arrogance, that is, with armed force and brutality. The Houthis occupied Sanaa and other than Sanaa, and arrest and kill on the pretext of "the popular revolution and the popular committees...", and America was supporting these moves of the Houthis politically and in terms of security. Politically, America does not consider the Houthis terrorists like al-Qaeda; rather, it considers them a political movement. The American Ambassador Matthew Tueller said in his press conference on 18/9/2014: "We distinguish between those groups that have participated in the political process; the Houthi movement participated in the National Dialogue Conference, and many positive results came out of that, and they have political positions and legitimate ambitions... Consequently, we support the Houthi and his movement in carrying out the same practices that political groups and parties carry out" (Muraqiboon Press website). As for security, when the Houthis entered Sanaa the army and police resisted them, and seven of the Houthis were killed on 9/9/2014, and the scales almost tipped in Hadi's favour, except that America hastened in a hurry to send Benomar, the United Nations envoy, "or in reality America's envoy", who pressured Hadi and diluted the matter with the call for negotiation, and gave the green light to the Houthis to escalate their movement during the atmosphere of negotiation, supported by the American pressures, in the person of Benomar, on Hadi..

5- Then the latest events confirm this support. I convey to you some of what came in the Answer to Question dated 27/3/2015 on this matter: (...America supplied the Houthis, by way of Iran, with kinds of weapons and equipment so that they could dominate Yemen by force, because it realises that the political milieu is for the most part creatures of the English... And thus the Houthis thought they had a force that would achieve for them domination over Yemen, so they besieged the President in order to take from him what they wanted through the laws he issues; he would agree and then procrastinate in implementation, until they imposed house arrest on him, and he escaped from them and went to Aden; they pursued him and he escaped from them a second time... America realised that its followers the Houthis had fallen into confusion; they had spread out in the country, and they could neither dominate nor return to the strength they had in their birthplace. So America saw fit to rescue them with a limited military action by which it would kill two birds with one stone: it would present them as victims of aggression after their aggression had become settled in people's minds, and it would create a pressing atmosphere of negotiation to obtain the compromise solution, as is its habit regarding what it cannot take alone... This became clear from following what has taken place and is taking place: Saudi Arabia consulted with America before the military action, and those carrying out the effective military role are America's agents, especially Salman, King of Saudi Arabia, and al-Sisi, the Egyptian President. As for the rest of the Gulf states, Jordan and Morocco, they are closer to the political role, in keeping with Britain's habit of going along with America so as to be in the picture and have a share in the intended negotiations, and to divide the cake of influence... And although pressing military actions sometimes succeed in opening the door of negotiation, they fail in it at other times, so matters become disturbed anew, and Yemen suffers from its fire, Yemen which was happy (Sa'id) on a day not long ago... a day when its pure land was not trodden by the agents and the Kafir colonialists.) End.

By contemplating what took place and its results, it becomes clear that America was the one controlling the course of matters. The focus of Saudi Arabia's attacks was on the weapons whose price the Muslims had paid, and the victims were mostly civilians and few of them were Houthis... And Iran did not intervene; rather, it remained watching from afar, even though voices were clamouring with the Decisive Storm falling on the heads of the Houthis!

This indicates that the maestro of the moves is controlling the rhythm so as to arrive at solutions that rescue the Houthis, not destroy them, and give them a share of consequence, not exclude them... and that Saudi Arabia realises that and runs its Storm of Decisiveness and of Hope according to this rhythm... and also that Iran realises that and watches without military intervention according to this rhythm...! Indeed, it agreed to the inspection of its ships carrying relief to Yemen before they reach the ports of Yemen, because America wants that, so Iran submitted...! Thus, just as Saudi Arabia is disciplined in its Decisiveness and its Hope according to the American directives, so too is Iran; both of them realise the purpose of these hot actions which we have explained. And here they are heading towards a hot calm that precedes the cold solutions!

6- In conclusion, Iran does not "break loose" from American policy; rather, it does not depart from it, and all of that on the pretext of common interest with the Great Satan!

Your brother, Ata Bin Khalil Abu al-Rashtah
